chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn Ameyra, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, who said:

We went to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so Hakam al-Sarraj said to him, 'What do you see regarding the one who carries the saddles and their equipment to Syria?' He said, 'There is no problem. You today are at the status of the companions of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). You are in a truce (hudna), so if the mutual exchange of tribute/gifts (mubayana) occurs, it will be prohibited upon you to carry the saddles and weapons to them.'

key_terms.السُّرُوج: Saddles (of camels), often used metonymically for goods or tribute
key_terms.الْمُبَايَنَة: Exchange of tribute or distinct political status

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on carrying weapons to Syria during the time of the Prophet's companions?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) uses the historical precedent of the Prophet’s companions to establish a dynamic legal framework for exporting arms to Syria, linking permissibility to the political status of 'hudna' (truce). This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the prohibition of sending weapons to non-Shia authorities is contingent upon the absence of a formal political allegiance or 'mubayana', rather than an absolute ban. It underscores the strategic nuance in Shia political thought regarding trade and military logistics during periods of relative peace.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Sayf Bin Ameyra, from Abu Bakr Al Hazramy who said,

‘We went over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so Hakam Al-Sarraj said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What do you<sup>asws</sup> see regarding the one who bears the saddles and their equipments to Syria?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem. Today you all are at the status of the companions of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>. You are in a truce, so if you were in the conflicts, it would have been Prohibited upon you that you should be carrying the saddles and the weapons to them’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Sayf ibn ‘Amirah from Abu Bakr al-Hadramiy who has said the following: “

Once, we visited abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and Hakam ibn al-Sarraj asked him (the Imam), ‘What is your decision about carrying saddles and things related to al-Sham (Syria)?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful. Today you are like the companions of the Messenger of Allah. You live in peace time. When there is hostility, then it is unlawful for you to carry to them saddles and arms to them.’”
